sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the mother of the petitioner had purchased the property by registered sale deed on 23.11.1987 and thereafter a settlement deed was issued in favour of the petitioner on 07.01.2009 by his mother,
which was registered as Doc.No.24/2009.
It was further submitted that the petitioner is paying water tax, property tax etc., and the petitioner is in possession and enjoyment of the property.
Apart from that, the petitioner has also given this property as security to the bank by memorandum of deposit of title deeds.

Therefore,
it was contended that there was no acquisition and the possession continues with the petitioner.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 18/07/2025 02:08:22 pm )
4. In the light of the stand taken by the 1st respondent in the counter, it is seen that acquisition proceedings were initiated and an award also came to be passed in Award No.8/86 dated 23.09.1986.

If according to the petitioner, the possession continues with the petitioner and the compensation amount has also not been paid, the petitioner must only question the acquisition proceedings by seeking for declaration that acquisition proceedings has lapsed.
Instead, the petitioner cannot seek for No objection certificate from the Housing Board.

Except giving this clarity, no further orders can be passed in the present writ petition.
5.
This writ petition is disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions, if any, are closed.
